Title: Continuous versus intermittent use of furosemide in patients with heart failure and moderate chronic renal dysfunction
Author: Zheng, Jiang, Chen, He, Xie, Lu
Comment: M_diff = 4.72 - 3.53 = 1.19 kg computed from the two explicitly reported arm means of a simple two-group between-subjects comparison (CI minus BI; positive favours continuous infusion). Dispersion ambiguity: the Statistical methods section and the Abstract state continuous variables are expressed as mean ± SD, whereas the legends of Tables 1 and 2 state "Values are mean ± SEM". Values were recorded as SD because treating them as SEM would be implausible (e.g. baseline body weight 58.65 ± 9.25 would imply SD ≈ 60 kg). N per arm (42 CI, 39 BI) is the final analysed/ITT N from the Table 2 header. 72 h period used (longest in-hospital period reported for weight; 48 h also reported).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Continuous infusion (CI) of intravenous furosemide over 6 h, no loading dose') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: randomized controlled trial (parallel, open-label, single centre)
domain: medicine / cardiology-nephrology (acute decompensated heart failure with chronic kidney disease)
Participant type: Adults (18-90 years) hospitalised with NYHA class III-IV acute decompensated heart failure and eGFR 15.0-44.9 mL/min/1.73 m2
Recruitment source: Nephrology Department, Zhejiang Hospital, Hangzhou, China (June 2016 - July 2019)
Outcome measurement: Mean body weight loss from baseline to 72 h, in kilograms (positive = weight lost)
effect_direction: favours continuous infusion (CI 4.72 kg vs BI 3.53 kg; MD +1.19 kg)

Report_ID: Net weight loss (kg) from admission to hospital day 3 or discharge
Title: Continuous Versus Bolus Dosing of Furosemide for Patients Hospitalized for Heart Failure
Author: Allen LA, Turer AT, DeWald T, Gattis Stough W, Cotter G, O'Connor CM
Comment: Paper reports weight change as negative for loss (bolus -1.64 ± 2.34; continuous -2.66 ± 2.44); signs reversed to positive kilograms lost per the synthesis plan, SDs unchanged. M_diff computed as group_2_mean − group_1_mean = 2.66 − 1.64 = 1.02 kg, oriented continuous minus bolus (MD > 0 favours continuous infusion). N analysed for weight not separately reported; randomised Ns per arm used (21 bolus, 20 continuous). Significance test used was Wilcoxon rank-sum (p = 0.27) although means ± SD are tabulated.
Participant type: adults hospitalized with acute decompensated heart failure and volume overload
Outcome measurement: Δ weight (kg), Table 2; sign reversed so values are positive kilograms lost
Outcome variable: Net weight loss (kg) from admission to hospital day 3 or discharge
effect_direction: favours continuous infusion (2.66 kg vs 1.64 kg lost; MD +1.02 kg, ns)

Report_ID: Net weight loss (kg) from enrollment to discharge
Title: Increased mortality in elderly heart failure patients receiving infusion of furosemide compared to elderly heart failure patients receiving bolus injection
Author: Sager R, Lindstedt I, Edvinsson L, Edvinsson ML
Comment: Values are within-group mean changes from enrollment to discharge (positive = kg lost), reported as mean ± SE (per table footnote), not SD; recorded in the SE fields. The paper reports no between-group test of weight CHANGE; the only between-group comparison is absolute weight at discharge (bolus 73.5 ± 4.2, n = 18 vs infusion 69.7 ± 3.3, n = 18, P = 0.48, Table 2). Period used = enrollment to discharge (~1 week, longest in-hospital period reported). n for the infusion weight-change row is 18 (18 of 20 randomised had discharge weight); bolus row n = 20 as printed in Table 3, although Table 2 lists n = 18 for bolus discharge weight — a possible inconsistency in the paper. M_diff not computed (left empty) because the two means come from separate within-group paired analyses rather than a reported between-group contrast.; treatment SD derived from its reported SE (SD = SE * sqrt(n)); control SD derived from its reported SE (SD = SE * sqrt(n))
Participant type: elderly hospitalised patients with severe heart failure (NYHA III-IV), mean age >80
Recruitment source: internal medicine ward, Skåne University Hospital, Lund, Sweden (January–September 2018)
Outcome measurement: Mean reduction in body weight (enrollment minus discharge), kilograms, reported as mean ± SE
Outcome variable: Net weight loss (kg) from enrollment to discharge
effect_direction: favours continuous infusion (1.43 kg vs 1.14 kg lost; no between-group test reported)

Title: Diuretic Strategies in Patients with Acute Decompensated Heart Failure (DOSE trial)
Author: Felker GM, et al.
Comment: Paper reports weight change as negative for loss (bolus -6.8±7.8 lb; continuous infusion -8.1±10.3 lb). Signs reversed to positive pounds lost per the synthesis plan; SDs unchanged. Values are in pounds — conversion factor to kilograms supplied (0.4535924, i.e. ÷2.205). Per-arm N analysed for weight change is not reported separately; randomised Ns (156 bolus, 152 continuous infusion) used. 2x2 factorial trial: the paper's own bolus-vs-continuous-infusion comparison already combines the low- and high-dose arms within each delivery mode, as required by the plan. M_diff not computed because these are factorial marginal means from a linear model adjusted for the other factor.
Participant type: adults hospitalised with acute decompensated heart failure on chronic oral loop diuretic therapy (80-240 mg furosemide equivalent/day)
Recruitment source: 26 clinical sites in the United States and Canada, March 2008 to November 2009 (NHLBI Heart Failure Clinical Research Network)
Outcome measurement: Change in weight at 72 hr — lb (Table 2); sign reversed so positive = pounds lost
effect_direction: favours continuous infusion (8.1 lb vs 6.8 lb lost; p=0.20)

Report_ID: Body weight loss, kg (baseline to compensated state)
Title: Comparison of three diuretic treatment strategies for patients with acute decompensated heart failure
Author: Yayla Ç, Akyel A, Canpolat U, et al.
Comment: The reported p=0.66 is the omnibus one-way ANOVA p-value across all three arms, not the pairwise cIV vs bI p-value. Ns are those randomised per arm (n analysed specifically for weight was not separately stated). M_diff left empty because the design is a three-arm trial and no pairwise cIV vs bI difference is reported by the paper. Note: the Methods text labels Tx1/Tx2 inconsistently with the Abstract and Tables; arm assignment here follows the Abstract/Table definitions (cIV = continuous infusion 160 mg/16 h, n=15; bI = bolus 80 mg twice daily, n=14).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Continuous intravenous infusion (cIV) of 160 mg furosemide over 16 h/day for 48 h') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Adults hospitalised with acute decompensated heart failure (pro-BNP > 300 pg/ml)
Recruitment source: Single centre, patients admitted to the emergency department within previous 24 h, Ankara, Turkey (March 2011 – November 2012)
Outcome measurement: Mean ± SD kilograms of body weight lost from baseline to compensated state (longest in-hospital period reported)
Outcome variable: Body weight loss, kg (baseline to compensated state)
additional_group_ns: Third arm not used for this comparison: furosemide 160 mg plus 150 ml 1.95% NaCl hypertonic saline solution (HSS) over 30 min once daily, n=14, body weight loss 5.7 ± 3.6 kg
effect_direction: favours continuous infusion (4.6 kg vs 4.1 kg lost; omnibus p=0.66)
